source_text.body:
Book travel with an AI agent
An author tested AI booking agents for travel; one ticket booking stalled at a human check and the agent asked for help. Another agent can rebook trips and apply credits.
Done with
MM
Meta Muse
What they did
Stefan Hawes asked Meta's Muse agent to find a weekend activity for his family in Berlin. It found a circus, located tickets and worked in German. Later he asked it to buy tickets to a basketball game. It stopped at the ticket site's prove-you-are-human check and asked him for help, so he bought the tickets himself.
How it went
Muse got him about 95% of the way on the circus booking, but failed at payment because his card was from Europe. The basketball purchase was blocked by the human check. Separately, Instinct is reported to rebook trips and apply credits.
Worth knowing
Muse was only available in the U.S. and Canada, and Hawes used a Canadian account. Expect a European card or a robot check to stop the final step.
Try it yourself
with
Operator
Copy prompt
Help me book [flight/train/hotel] from [origin] to [destination] on [dates] for [number] travelers, with a budget of [amount] and preferences of [seat, airline, times, etc.]. Search a few sites, then show me the best 2-3 options with prices and conditions. Pause and show me the full details before entering any payment info or confirming a booking, and if you hit a human check or login, stop and ask me to take over.
Original source: https://resonanceco.com/insights/ai-agents-have-started-booking-travel-will-they-choose-your-destination/
